question: From 2013 to 2025, how many pedestrians were killed in motor vehicle crashes in NYC each year?

options.reason: Bars make it easy to compare the discrete yearly death totals directly.
options.interpretation: The bars give the annual pedestrian death count for every year in the requested period, with 2013 highest at 176 and 2020 lowest at 101. Annual totals directly answer the question; they do not indicate pedestrian risk per trip or population because no exposure denominator is included.

options.reason: A line chart emphasizes how the yearly counts change over time while retaining the value for each year.
options.interpretation: The connected annual counts show a general decline from 176 in 2013 to 119 in 2025, with year-to-year fluctuations and a low of 101 in 2020. This is a defensible time-series view of the full annual-count question; it leaves pedestrian risk relative to travel or population unanswered because those denominators are not in the data.

answer:
The bar-chart framing shows 176 pedestrians killed in 2013, 133 in 2014, 133 in 2015, 149 in 2016, 127 in 2017, 123 in 2018, 131 in 2019, 101 in 2020, 132 in 2021, 135 in 2022, 107 in 2023, 124 in 2024, and 119 in 2025.
The line-chart framing shows the same annual counts: 176 in 2013, 133 in 2014, 133 in 2015, 149 in 2016, 127 in 2017, 123 in 2018, 131 in 2019, 101 in 2020, 132 in 2021, 135 in 2022, 107 in 2023, 124 in 2024, and 119 in 2025.
